data.text:
# Hyperbolic Lanterns
Ray tracing in hyperbolic space: the order-5 cubic honeycomb {4,3,5}, a spinning cube in every cell casting volumetric light cones. Rays cross cells by Lorentz reflections in the hyperboloid model.
Reacts to music: open the audio menu → Mic (each beat ripples outward through the honeycomb).
## Tweak it in the Parameters panel
Press P (or the sliders button in the top bar): Cells, Light, Post and Music settings with pretty names; hover a name for what it does, double-click a slider to reset it.
Double-click a group box to open it, Esc to come back.

## Cell Geometry
Cube size, cone angle and echo (how much each reflected cell keeps) of the honeycomb, plus the centered screen UV the camera rays start from.

## Lantern Palette
Two lantern colors whose hues drift slowly with time (Hue Shift by time × 0.015).

## Render Targets
Feedback nodes used as render targets: the tonemapped frame (for chromatic aberration) and a bright pass (luma smoothstep) for bloom and streaks.

## Bloom
Two blur radii of the bright pass added together, plus a tinted horizontal anamorphic streak.

## Music
Audio level gates everything: with the audio off or silent, drive = 0 and the piece looks exactly as before. drive = music × smoothstep(level).
- Beat ripple: inside the honeycomb, each beat is delayed by distance (ripple = 0.35 beats per unit), so a wavefront rolls outward: lamp cores and cube edges flare, the light cones light up in a shell, and the cubes surge forward in their spin.
- Bass: light-cone intensity breathes up to +35%.
Beat-phase couplings (the ripple flare, cone shell and spin surge inside Hyperbolic Honeycomb) are also multiplied by the beat tracker's confidence (Beat.confidence = u_beatConfidence: 0 with the audio off, ~1 once the beat locks, 1 with the metronome) and run on the stable beat clock with its certainty gate (x smoothstep(0.25, 0.75, u_beatTrust) in the shader): after a track change the clock holds the old tempo, then glides to the new one without jumps, and these couplings fade out until the new beat is trusted. Level and band couplings (bass cone breathing) are not.
